title: Residential Painting in Micanopy, FL | Pre-War Homes
description: Residential painting in Micanopy, FL for pre-war homes and newer houses: careful scraping, rot repair, flexible caulk, and premium paint inside and out.
h1: Residential Painting for Micanopy's Pre-War and Newer Homes
heroIntro: Repainting an older Micanopy house is mostly about what happens before the paint. We take the time on scraping, repair, and caulking that pre-war homes need, then finish them inside and out.

questions: How is painting an old house different from painting a new one?
Should rotted wood be replaced before painting?
How long does it take to repaint a pre-war home?

sections.h2: Why older homes take more care
body: Micanopy's pre-war homes have been repainted many times. Each layer was applied by a different crew with a different product, and over decades those layers crack, lift, and lose their bond to the wood. Spraying a fresh coat on top just adds weight to a film that is already failing. A lasting residential painting job in Micanopy, FL has to start by finding the sound layer and working back to it.

Older houses also move. Wood siding, window casings, and porch framing swell and shrink with the seasons, which is why rigid old caulk splits and why we use flexible, paintable sealants on every moving joint.

bullets: Hand-scrape loose paint to a firm edge and feather-sand so the transitions do not telegraph
Probe sills, door frames, and lower siding for soft wood and replace what has rotted
Set nail pops and re-secure loose boards
Cut out failed caulk and re-lay flexible sealant
Spot-prime bare wood and any knots or tannin bleed
body: On an older house, prep days can be the biggest share of the schedule. The estimate spells out every step so you know where the time goes.

Interiors in older Micanopy homes often have tall ceilings, deep trim, original doors, and walls with years of patching. We protect floors and furniture, repair cracks and dents, and choose sheens that suit the room: flatter on walls where light rakes across old surfaces, harder enamels on doors, trim, and railings. You can stay home while we work room by room. More on that side is on our Micanopy interior painting page.

sections.h2: Newer homes in the Micanopy area
body: Not every house in the area is historic. We also repaint more recent homes, whether in town, near Tuscawilla Preserve, or along the McIntosh corridor, where the work tends to center on faded south and west walls, builder-grade interior paint, and mildew in shaded spots. The same system applies: wash, repair, caulk, prime, and two full coats.

A pre-war home usually looks best in a palette that respects its age. Our article on historic paint colors is a good starting point, and a color consultation in Micanopy puts full-size samples on your walls under the oak-filtered light. See also our main residential painting page.

faqs.q: Can you just paint over the old paint on my historic home?
faqs.a: Only where it is still firmly bonded. Loose and lifting paint is scraped back to a sound edge first, because new paint cannot hold failing layers in place.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted siding and trim?
faqs.a: Yes. Rot and fascia replacement is part of our prep, and it is listed on the estimate before any work starts.

faqs.q: How long will an exterior repaint take on an older Micanopy house?
faqs.a: A full exterior typically takes three to seven working days plus wash and dry time. Older homes with heavy prep and lots of trim tend toward the longer end.
